mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals monetary easing, reducing equity discount rates and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through lower cost of capital for corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1% (as of t-1mo) over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 9.0% indicates severe labor market weakness, reducing consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 9.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and real consumption (RSAFS) signal broad demand contraction, triggering equity sell-offs as corporate revenue expectations fall over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by >1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: In post-crisis supply recovery regimes, rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals manufacturing sector strength, boosting corporate earnings visibility and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO rises above its 6-month moving average during recovery.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month indicates labor market strength, supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.0% triggers expectations of monetary tightening, increasing equity discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in housing starts (HOUST) and real GDP growth (GDPC1) signal systemic demand collapse, reducing corporate revenue outlook and generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and GDPC1 decline by >0.5% quarter-over-quarter.

mechanism_narrative: In housing recovery regimes, rising housing starts (HOUST) above 12-month moving average signals improving consumer confidence and economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises above its 12-month moving average during recovery.
